title: RDMBench manufacturer PID table
description: One brand's manufacturer-specific PID names and types — the file format under `manufacturer-pids/` and what `export-pids --out` writes. Sourced from manuals, the fixture's own PARAMETER_DESCRIPTION, or sniffing; never from OLA's PID store.

manufacturer_id.description: ESTA manufacturer ID — the top 16 bits of the brand's UIDs.

source.description:
Where these entries came from. Required by the sourcing rule, and
the first thing to check when an entry looks wrong on a bench.

wanted.description:
PIDs this brand's fixtures list but will not describe, and that no
table names — the library's own to-do list, per brand.

A bench ignores these: they name nothing, so nothing changes in a
report. They are here for the curator with a manual open, and they
ride on the table file because a capture is one file and a pull
request proposing it is one click. A fixture that describes nothing
but lists ten private PIDs is the most useful thing a tech can send
and used to be the one capture that produced no file at all.

EnumValue.description:
One named value of an enumerated manufacturer parameter, from
ENUM_LABEL (§10.4.3).

HexU16.description: 16-bit value as `0xABCD` (a bare `ABCD` or a plain number is accepted on read).

labels.description:
Names for the values of an enumerated PID. Only ever what a fixture
said through ENUM_LABEL (§10.4.3) — a captured file carries them
so a unit that names its values once names them for every later
bench that meets the same brand. Not a place for hand-written
interpretation; that is what the knowledge packs are for.

metadata_version.description:
The fixture's E1.37-5 §5 metadata description, verbatim, with its
version. Carried for the record and for the curator who merges a
capture — the snapshot only ever reads it from the fixture itself.
